dedupe_keys.name: montana mesonet weather and soil moisture station network

description: The Montana Mesonet is a network of weather and soil moisture stations run by the Montana Climate Office at the University of Montana, grown from 6 stations installed in 2016 to over 215 active stations, with 128 of a further 205 stations funded by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers already installed about every 500 square miles in central and eastern Montana. Its AgriMet stations, aimed at precision agriculture, measure air temperature, humidity, solar radiation, wind, rainfall and soil temperature and water content at 10, 20, 50 and 90 cm, while HydroMet stations serve hydrology and carry cameras photographing the landscape, sky and snowpack. Coverage is the state of Montana. Current conditions are shown on an interactive map, and data are served free through an API, spatial services, an app and an open-source dashboard built with Plotly Dash; the page read states no licence. Caveats: station density is uneven, since stations depend on landowners, tribes, agencies and grants, and records start in 2016 at the earliest. For simulation it supplies observed soil moisture and weather to drive drought assessments, crop and rangeland models and flood forecasts for farms, water supply and roads in the northern Great Plains. It is related to the USDA Climate Hubs adaptation workbook case studies record in this catalogue.
